title: RNA isolation with TRIzol
author: Magdalena Julkowska

steps_raw.instruction: Add 1 ml of TRIzol per 30-50 mg of tissue material
Incubate for 5 minutes to permit complete dissociation of the nucleoproteins complex
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol™ Reagent used for lysis, then securely cap the tube.
Centrifuge the sample for 15 minutes at max speed - room temperature
Transfer the aqueous phase containing the RNA to a new tube.
Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase, per 1 mL of TRIzol™ Reagent used for lysis
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at max speed at room temperature
Discard the supernatant with a pipette
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol used for lysis.
Vortex the sample breflly then centrifuge for 5 minutes at max speed at room temperature
Discard the supernatant with a pipette
Vacuum or air dry the RNA pellet for 5–10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 20–50 µL of RNase-free water by pipetting up and down.
Determine RNA concentration using the nanodrop
